extracted.intended_audience: educators, teachers, curriculum designers, and educational theorists
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts practical and theoretical criteria for organizing school instruction so learning arises from purposeful activity, experience, and reflective thinking rather than isolated drill. Emphasizes linking subject matter, bodily activity, and reflection to real ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline as constructive power of achievement
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline should be identified with growth in constructive power of achievement rather than mere strain or application for its own sake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Will involves effort directed toward future consequences; equating discipline with mere application or 'strain' is a negative conception. Anti-pattern: treating application for its own sake as Discipline (e.g., 'application just for the sake of application... is alone disciplinary'). If pupil fails, the fault should not automatically be seen as lack of discipline in the pupil when the material or methods may be at fault.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter must be tied to active lines of interest and purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: A fact or truth becomes an object of study only when it figures as a factor in carrying forward active lines of interest or in completing purposeful activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbers or other topics are to be learned insofar as they represent qualities and relations relevant to actions and purposes. Effectual study is when the pupil realizes the place of the content in activities that concern them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid isolation of subject matter into independent branches
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional curriculum that treats history, algebra, geography, etc., as separate, complete branches for their own sake is misguided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such isolation makes subject matter independent of the learner's interests and purposes; curriculum should instead show how topics function as resources or obstacles in continuous intentional pursuits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize education to enlist natural active tendencies in purposeful doing
rubrics_metrics.description: Education should provide an environment that induces activity in doing something while ensuring the doing requires observation, acquisition of information, and constructive imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reorganization is piecemeal but necessary; avoid nominal acceptance of one philosophy while practicing another. The aim is to have learning take place in connection with intelligent carrying forward of purposeful activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest and discipline are correlative aspects of purposive activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Interest means identification with the objects that define an activity; discipline is the development of continuous attention (will) that grows from such interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both interest and discipline arise from activities that have an aim; fostering interest properly leads to genuine discipline — not the mere mechanical enforcement of attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experience comprises both active (trying) and passive (undergoing) elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Experience is 'trying' (experimenting) and 'undergoing' (suffering consequences); their connection measures the fruitfulness of the experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a child sticking his finger into a flame is not having experience unless the action is connected with the pain consequence; 'learning from experience' requires the backward-and-forward connection between deed and consequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of experience lies in perception of relationships and continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: An experience counts insofar as it leads to perception of relationships or continuities and is cumulative — i.e., it 'amounts to something' that can be carried over.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experience that is merely a sequence of unconnected events yields no learning; 'an ounce of experience is better than a ton of theory' because experience gives theory vital and verifiable significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dualism of mind and body; integrate bodily activity into learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Separating 'mind' from bodily activity makes physical actions an intruder or distraction; bodily activity should be organized as part of meaningful occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-patterns include rigid silence, enforced quiescence, and suppression of movement leading to strain and callousness. Positive example: Greek education did not separate mind and body; bodily energies should be used constructively rather than merely suppressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use senses and motor training as organic participants, not mere conduits
rubrics_metrics.description: Senses and muscles should be employed as integral parts of doing with a purpose, not merely as channels for conveying information to a separate 'mind.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: flying a kite requires eye and hand perception tied to action; when reading or spelling is taught as isolated form-identification, the sensory-motor technique becomes mechanical and divorced from meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mechanical separation of acts from purpose (mechanical habits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques taught in isolation (e.g., rote reading, calculation drills, laboratory exercises done for their own sake) produce mechanical habits that are hard to reattach to meaning later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This narrow motor/sensory training makes later intelligent use difficult; teachers urging 'read with expression' cannot overcome earlier mechanical training that ignored meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perception is inherently relational and involves judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Perception and ideas are not mere inventories of isolated qualities; genuine perception discerns bearings, uses, causes, and relations (e.g., a chair is known by its relation to purpose, not a list of parts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educational aim should be to cultivate discernment of relationships rather than accumulation of disconnected perceptions or facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Words must not substitute for real ideas (avoid pseudo-ideas)
rubrics_metrics.description: When mental activity is separated from active concern, words and symbols easily take the place of ideas, producing half-observations and verbal formulas that obscure genuine perception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning: accepting minimal or pseudo-meaning in words prevents deeper observation; theory apart from experience becomes a mere catchword.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflection (thinking) is the discernment of relations between action and consequence
rubrics_metrics.description: Thinking consists in intentionally seeking the specific connections between what we do and what happens, thereby making activity and consequence continuous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflection extends simple trial-and-error by analyzing links; it increases foresight and practical control because one can identify antecedent conditions and supply or remove them as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate reflective experience rather than mere cut-and-try
rubrics_metrics.description: While trial-and-error finds a working method, reflective experience analyzes why it works; this reflective quality changes the nature and value of the experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflective experience enables deliberate methods, explanation, and reasoning about actions rather than crude, circumstance-dependent routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thinking requires problematic, incomplete situations and involves inquiry and hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Thought arises when situations are doubtful or incomplete; it is a process of inquiry involving conjecture, tentative hypotheses, risk, and revision rather than dogmatic certainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples/illustrations: the Greek dilemma about knowing vs ignorance, wartime decision-making, and the historian's account. Teaching should foster the use of doubt to guide inquiry and experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance personal identification with impartial detachment in reflection
rubrics_metrics.description: Although thinking originates in a personal share of consequences (interest, desire), valuable reflection must cultivate a degree of detachment to prevent biasing observations and inferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paradox: reflection is born of partiality but must achieve impartiality; educators should help learners retain motive to inquire while training them to keep preferences from distorting data and reasoning.
